report.summary: Chunk 2 of fanout.py: defines FanoutResult dataclass, _one_call function, and safe_key generation logic. Claims about secret_floor_rule and trace_id are uncheckable.
risks: safe_key | medium | The safe_key function uses a 10-character SHA-256 digest, which is not collision-resistant for large numbers of task IDs. This could cause key collisions in rare cases. | Review the number of expected task IDs and consider using a longer digest or a different approach.

handoff.purpose: Defines safe_key method, FanoutResult dataclass, and _one_call function.

claims.text: A name that looks like an attack invites someone to "harden" it later by a route that breaks resume.
claims.why: This is a design rationale; no code to verify.

claims.text: ``policy`` is handed to the provider, which passes it to :func:`daedalus.sensitivity.classify_data`.
claims.why: The code passes policy to provider.run(); the claim about classify_data is in another module.

claims.text: It cannot lift the secret floor. ``providers/deepseek.py`` calls :func:`secret_floor_rule` per path independently of ``classify_data``, and that rule is documented as running "in EVERY lane, no bypass ... cannot be weakened by a project config".
claims.why: References providers/deepseek.py and secret_floor_rule, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Verified with a fully permissive policy: source files pass, ``.env`` is still refused.
claims.why: No test or verification code in this chunk.

claims.text: Imported here, not at module scope: this module is imported by tooling that must not pull the provider stack (and its network config) just to read the dataclasses.
claims.why: The import of DeepSeekProvider is inside the function body, not at module level.

claims.text: BEFORE the question, not after. A model that has already read the question treats the brief as supporting material; a model that reads the brief first treats the question as being about the thing described.
claims.why: The code prepends brief to objective before passing to provider.run().

claims.text: fresh per call -- see module docstring
claims.why: Module docstring not in this chunk.

claims.text: The drift detector in tests/test_envelope_coverage.py caught this module as an undeclared record producer on 2026-07-30 and it was right: these files record a PAID external call and its answer, so a trace id correlates a bill to the run that incurred it.
claims.why: References test file and external event not in this chunk.

claims.text: From :func:`daedalus.spine.envelope.current_trace_id`, which NEVER mints -- so None means "no trace was in scope", not "here is a fresh unrelated id".
claims.why: References daedalus.spine.envelope.current_trace_id, not in this chunk.

observations.what: safe_key uses a 10-character SHA-256 digest, which may not be collision-resistant for large numbers of task IDs.
_one_call imports DeepSeekProvider inside the function to avoid module-level import of provider stack.
The docstring of _one_call makes multiple claims about behavior in other modules (classify_data, secret_floor_rule) that cannot be verified in this chunk.
